column2: req_desc

First steps from the title screen
From a grading world, signed in as `explorer`, a keyboard-only session plays with Wump, opens play through `Start walking`, walks, runs, jumps and orbits as published, and after reload `data-tile` still reads the saved tile.

Title screen Tab order
Pressing Tab through the title screen reaches its controls in exactly the order printed in Interactions, for the signed-in and the signed-out header.

Guide creature keyboard control
With `application "Guide creature"` focused, ArrowRight twice gives `data-spin="30"`, + gives `data-zoom="1.25"`, Space gives `data-nudges="1"`, and `Guide status` announces each result with its published template.

Guide creature pointer pull
A pointer drag on `Guide creature` changes `data-spin` and raises `data-stretch`, and after release `data-stretch` springs back to `0.00` within 600 ms of page time.

Published walk and run steps
From spot 1, holding D for 400 ms of page time ends on tile 5,12, and then R with D held for 400 ms ends on 9,12, with `data-step`, `data-tile`, `data-heading` and `data-gait` matching the movement rule after every step.

Rock stop and jump
From tile 7,5 on Saltmarsh Harbour, holding S stops at the rock with `data-heading="S"`, and Space lands on 7,7 on the fourth step with `data-gait="jump"` until it lands.

Explore camera keys and focus scope
In explore mode Q, E, + and Home change `data-yaw` and `data-zoom` as the keyboard table says, and after Tab leaves `World view`, pressing D moves nothing.

Phone expedition
At 375x812 with touch, an explorer walks by joystick, runs and jumps by button, walks by map tap, closes the sheets and keeps a photo using only `Camera`, `Zoom in`, `Focus` and `Take photo`.

Joystick holds a direction
At 375x812, a touch that starts on `group "Joystick"` and moves at least 16 px north, held for 400 ms of page time, walks exactly 2 tiles north, and lifting the finger stops it.

Run and Jump by tap
At 375x812, tapping `button "Run"` sets its `aria-pressed` and makes a 400 ms joystick hold cover 4 tiles, and tapping `button "Jump"` runs the published four-step jump.

Tapped map tile walks the published path
Tapping tile 12,10 on the `Island map` from spot 1 walks the published shortest path, and `data-tile` reads each published tile after its step.

Two-finger orbit and pinch
In explore mode on `World view`, two touches moving sideways change `data-yaw` by 1 degree per 2 px of midpoint movement, rightward adding and leftward subtracting, and each 40 px of pinch steps `data-zoom`, including through 1, 2 and 4 in photo mode.

Phone sheets close completely
At 375x812 the map, album and photo result open as full-width bottom sheets, and `Close map`, `Close album` and `Close` leave them hidden, out of the accessibility tree and out of the Tab order with focus back on the opener.

Published layouts at three viewports
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 the layouts printed in Screens and layout appear, including 44 px targets, no horizontal overflow, and at 768x1024 the Joystick shown only with a coarse pointer.

Keyboard photo from a deep link
Opening `/play?island=1&spot=2` and using only keys, an explorer enters photo mode, sets zoom 2, takes worked example 1, closes the result and sees the page filled in the album opened with J.

Entering photo mode by keyboard
C sets `data-mode="photo"`, `data-yaw` to the heading's angle, `data-zoom="1"` and `data-focus="4"` at once, with `data-in-view="mossback-newt"` at spot 2 and the matching `Frame guide` message.

Turning changes the frame guide
In photo mode at spot 2, E turns the explorer east and `Frame guide` reads its no-creature message with `data-in-view` empty, and Q turns it back so the newt message returns, with `data-tile` unchanged.

Scoring pending and one announcement
While the photo request is held, `Photo status` holds only its scoring message, and after release it announces the published result template exactly once and `dialog "Photo result"` opens.

Score figures count up
After a kept photo the `score-total` figure reads strictly between 0 and 100 at 300 ms of page time and `100 / 100` at 600 ms for worked example 1, and the row figures end on 30, 25, 25 and 20.

Result survives the world
`dialog "Photo result"` stays open with its text intact through clock, weather and live events, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, and Escape closes it with focus back on `World view`.

Album shows only a stored photo
After worked example 1 the album shows the newt page filled with `4 of 4 pages` and an image from the app's origin, the player's second tab shows it live, and the MinIO object is byte-identical to the uploaded image.

Scored examples by keyboard poses
Worked examples 1, 3 and 4, reached by deep link, keys and the clock route, show the published rows and totals in `Photo result`, and the API answers on the wire carry the same numbers.

Worked examples and refusal order on the API
All five worked examples through `POST /api/photos` answer `201` with the published scores, and combined faults answer with the single refusal the published photo error order selects.

Rewritten poses are refused
With the page's outgoing pose rewritten to water tile 15,4, a tick 31 behind, or a camera 2 tiles away, `Photo status` shows that refusal's exact message, no result opens, nothing is stored and the `film` figure stays.

Nothing in frame is refused
From spot 1 facing E at tick 6000, taking a photo by keyboard shows the `nothing_in_frame` message in `Photo status` with no photo row, no object and an unchanged film figure.

One shot key makes one photo
Repeating the page's Take request under its `Shot-Key` returns the first answer and spends one frame, a reused key with another pose answers the `shot_key_reused` 409, and the `film` figure matches the ledger after reload.

Two presses keep one photo
Two Enter presses in photo mode within 100 ms of page time send one request and leave one `photos` row and one spent frame.

Interleaved players keep their own answers
Two players taking photos at the same time in separate contexts each see only their own creature, total and film count in `Photo status` and `Photo result`, whatever order the requests finish in.

One world on two screens
`explorer` and `friend` in one grading world watch the clock move through morning, dusk and rain, and at each stop both `World view` elements report the same `data-tick`, `data-weather` and `data-creatures`.

Same tick and creatures on both screens
At tick 6000 both contexts on Saltmarsh Harbour show `data-tick="6000"` and `data-creatures="mossback-newt@12,6,S;reedpipe-heron@6,16,E"`.

Clock change arrives with the page clock paused
After the clock route moves to tick 6030, both pages show `reedpipe-heron@9,16,E` in `data-creatures` within 2 seconds of real time, with their page clocks still paused.

The device clock is ignored
A context whose page clock is set years away and whose time zone differs still shows `data-world-hour="10"`, `timer "World time"` `10:00` and `data-weather="clear"` at tick 6000.

Dusk arrives from the server
At tick 11000 `World status` announces the dusk message, `data-world-hour="18"`, the moth appears in `data-creatures` and in `data-in-view` from spot 4, and a scene capture differs from the one at 10:00.

Rain arrives from the server
At tick 4000 `World status` announces the rain message, `data-weather="rain"` and `puddle-lark@4,4,S` appears in `data-creatures`, and a later clock move out of the rain hours announces its end and removes the lark.

Route rule on the world API
`GET /api/world` reports each creature's position and heading by the published route rule at several ticks, lists dusk-only and rain-only creatures only in their hours and ignores any tick the client sends.

The last stamp opens the lighthouse
Tab A photographs the newt as worked example 1 and tab B of the same player shows the new page, stamp and open lighthouse live, then a keyboard restart resets both while photos and the hall stay.

Page, stamp and lighthouse announcements
That photo announces the album-page message in `Photo status` and the stamp and lighthouse messages in `World status`, and `data-lighthouse` becomes `open`.

Other tab follows stamps
Tab B's `stamps` figure reads `3 stamps` after its count-up and its `data-lighthouse` reads `open`, with no reload and no change of focus.

Film figure equals the paired ledger
The `film` figure counts from `30 frames` to `35 frames`, strictly between at 300 ms of page time, every `film_ledger` change is a pair summing to zero, the satchel sum equals the figure, and `Refill film` restores 36 on Saltmarsh Harbour only.

Album tabs by keyboard
J opens the album with focus on `tablist "Islands"`, arrow keys move across its tabs and change the shown island's `album-pages` figure, and Escape returns focus to `World view`.

Restart confirmation by keyboard
`Restart expedition` opens `alertdialog "Restart the expedition?"` with its published sentence, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside, and Escape or `Keep playing` closes it with focus back on the opener and nothing changed.

Restart reaches every tab and the text world
Confirming `Restart` puts album counts, stamps, the lighthouse, film and position back as published in both tabs within 2 seconds, keeps photos and the hall, and `/text-world` shows the same counts as the API.

A friend visits and likes a hall
`explorer` reorders and saves a hall, `friend` walks it, views and likes a photo, and `explorer`'s open hall page shows the new count and hears the like without a reload.

Reorder the hall by keyboard
On `/hall`, Alt+ArrowDown on the focused heron item moves it to frame 2, `Gallery status` announces the move message, focus stays on the item, and `Save hall` keeps the order after reload.

Walk a hall by keys
On `/hall/<handle>`, holding W for 400 ms of page time with `application "Gallery hall"` focused moves `data-tile` from 2,13 to 2,11, and the outer walls stop it.

Photo viewer by keyboard
`View Reedpipe heron photo` opens `dialog "Photo viewer"` by keyboard, + raises its `data-zoom` from 1 to 2, and Escape closes it with focus back on the opener.

Like counts move in place
When `friend` likes a photo, `explorer`'s `likes` figure reaches `1 like` after its count-up with no reload and no loss of scroll position or focus, and `Gallery status` announces the like message once.

One like per visitor and request-scoped readers
A repeat like from a second `friend` tab leaves one `likes` row, unliking shows `0 likes` live, and interleaved hall reads by owner and visitors each return the reader's own `liked_by_me`, film count and account menu.

Public hall switch
Turning `switch "Public hall"` off makes that hall answer 404 for `friend` on reload, in the API and for the images shown only there, and turning it on restores them.

A friend takes the guest seat
`friend` joins `explorer`'s safari by code and follows the host's walking, sightings and photos live while `rival` is refused the seat, and after `friend` leaves `rival` can join.

Join a safari by keyboard
`dialog "Join a safari"` opens, accepts a typed code with Enter, shows `no_safari`'s message in `Safari status` for a wrong code with focus kept in the field, joins on the right code, and returns focus to its opener when closed.

Host position arrives live
On the guest's `World view`, `data-host-island` and `data-host-tile` follow each tile the host walks within 2 seconds, with no reload and no change of the guest's own tile.

Sightings by map keyboard
The host moves the map cursor with arrows and presses S, and both players' `list "Sightings"` gain the published sighting line in place and `Safari status` announces it.

Host photos reach the guest
Each photo the host keeps appears in the guest's `log "Safari feed"` as its published line with an image from the app's origin, without moving the guest's focus or closing an open panel.

One winner for the last seat
When `friend` and `rival` join the same safari at once, one gets the seat and the other sees the `safari_full` message in `Safari status` with the API answering 409, and the seat count stays at one guest.

A closed guest page frees its seat and connection
On `short-limits`, closing the guest's page frees the seat no earlier than 3 seconds and no later than 6 seconds after it closes, the host hears the left message, `rival` can join, and after ten streams closed mid-way no app session stays active or idle in transaction.

A note reaches the board through a ranger
`explorer` pins a note by keyboard, `ranger` approves it, and `friend`'s open board shows it live; `ranger` also declines `friend`'s pending note and `friend` is told why.

Pin a note by keyboard, shown as typed Pinning `Low tide **today**` by keyboard shows those literal characters with `Waiting for a ranger` to the author only, two presses leave one pending note, and a half-typed draft stays intact through live events.

Approved notes arrive live
After `ranger` approves by keyboard on `/ranger`, `friend`'s open `list "Notice board"` shows the note within 2 seconds with its characters exactly as typed and `Notes status` announces the new-note message.

Decline by keyboard with a reason
`dialog "Decline note"` works by keyboard, Escape returns focus to the note's `Decline`, and confirming `Shares personal details` sends the author the published declined message live.

Two rangers on one note
When `ranger` and `ranger2` decide one note, the first decision stands, the API answers the second with the `note_decided` 409, and the second ranger's `Notes status` shows the message naming the outcome and first ranger.

Note length limit
Typing and pinning 141 characters shows the `note_too_long` message in `Notes status` and stores nothing, and exactly 140 characters is accepted.

Unconfirmed players cannot pin
`newcomer` pressing `Pin note` sees the `unconfirmed` message in `Notes status`, the API answers 403, and no note row is stored.

Postcard to someone with no account
`explorer` posts the moth photo to an address, one message arrives, and a signed-out context opens its link and reads the image, creature, score, island and line.

Post by keyboard once
`dialog "Send postcard"` works by keyboard, two presses of Post make one postcard and one Mailpit message, and `Postcard status` announces the posted message once only after Mailpit accepted it.

Postcard message content
The Mailpit message has the published sender, subject, text body, link and attachment, with the line exactly as typed including `<i>`, and the sender's address appears nowhere in it.

Public postcard page
In a signed-out context `/postcards/<id>` shows the image from the app's origin and the published fields as literal text, with the sender's address absent from the page and its API answer.

Postcard with storage unreachable
On `storage-down`, pressing Post shows the postcard storage message in `Postcard status`, the API answers 503, no message reaches Mailpit and no postcard is stored as posted.

Postcard rate limit
On `short-limits`, the third postcard shows the `postcard_limit` message with the limit 2 in `Postcard status`, and the API answers 429 with `Retry-After` in seconds.

Confirmation code by mail
`newcomer` gets the `unconfirmed` message on Post, presses `Send a new code`, reads the six-digit code from Mailpit, types it on `/confirm`, and can then post.

Board re-ranks as players enter
`explorer` and `friend` enter their heron photos over `rival`'s seeded entry, both open boards re-rank in place, and a filter then narrows the list.

Enter a photo by keyboard
`dialog "Enter a photo"` opens, selects `radio "Reedpipe heron photo, 74"` and submits by keyboard, focus returns to `Enter a photo`, and the player's row appears without a reload.

Ranking and tie break move in place
`friend`'s 74 at tick 5100 ranks above `explorer`'s 74 at tick 5200 on every open board within 2 seconds, with `Board status` announcing the update message for `friend` at number 1.

Filter waits for the last keystroke
Typing in `searchbox "Filter players"` sends one `GET /api/boards/1?player=<text>` 250 ms of page time after the last key, none before, and `Board status` shows the published filtered message.

An older filter answer is ignored
With the answer for an older input held and released last, only the latest input's rows and message stay on screen.

A failed board load stays visible
When a board load fails, `Board status` shows its failure message and keeps it through later timers and live events until a new load succeeds.

The browser cannot set a board score
Adding a score to the outgoing entry request changes nothing, and each row's score, the entry count and the API all equal the `photos` row's total.

The whole photo journey with reduced motion
Under reduced motion an explorer keeps worked example 1, reads the result, then follows the same player's sail in a text-world tab, with every task completed and the end states published for normal motion.

Photo mode cuts under reduced motion
Under reduced motion C and Home make `data-mode`, `data-yaw`, `data-zoom` and `data-camera` final on the next frame, with `data-guide="drawn"` and no glide.

Shutter and figures under reduced motion
Under reduced motion taking a photo starts no running animation on `World view` or its overlays, `data-shutter` stays `idle`, and each figure shows its final text at once with the same `Photo status` announcement.

Stillness under reduced motion
With the explorer idle and the tick unchanged, two scene captures 1 second of page time apart are identical, and Space on `Guide creature` raises `data-nudges` and announces with no hop and `data-stretch` at `0.00`.

Text world follows the explorer live
With `/text-world` open in a second tab, `Sail to Fernhollow` updates its location line and announces it in `Text world status` within 2 seconds, without a reload or a change of focus.

Still fallback without WebGL
Without WebGL `/play` sets `data-state="still"`, shows `img "Still map of Saltmarsh Harbour"`, the exact notice from Feedback states and text-world content with the same progress as the API.

Text world content and access
`/text-world` shows every island heading and published creature and progress line, has no axe violations, and its `Refill film` and sail buttons work with no 3D scene.

Sound, settings and links in one visit
One visit turns sound on and off, saves settings, follows deep links and Back, and survives a sign-in round trip, with every request from `/play` going to the app's own origin.

Sound starts only on request
Before `button "Sound"` is pressed no audio context, source or gain exists; one press makes the published graph with master gain 1 and `aria-pressed="true"`, the next sets master gain 0, and each reload starts off.

Settings by keyboard
Setting `Music volume` to 40 by ArrowLeft and `Graphics` to `Light` by keyboard and saving announces the saved message, a second context after reload shows them with `data-preset="light"`, and `?gfx=balanced` overrides one load without saving.

Deep links, sailing and Back
`/play?island=3&spot=2` opens on Driftglass Reef at 12,10 facing N and survives reload, sailing adds a history entry, and Back returns to the earlier island and tile without a page reload.

Sign-in round trip and unknown spots
A signed-out visit to a deep link returns to that exact path after signing in, a non-local `next` lands on `/play`, and an unknown spot shows the published notice with the address replaced.

Private halls answer 404 everywhere
For everyone but `rival`, `rival`'s private hall shows the heading `No gallery here`, and its API, its like route and the image of `rival_private` answer 404.

Play continues with storage unreachable
On `storage-down`, a photo shows the photo storage message in `Photo status` with film and storage unchanged, D still walks, the map, album text and text world work, and `GET /api/health` answers 200 with `unavailable`.

The landing page performs the product
The title page shows the split headline around a live 35% wide viewfinder on an otherwise empty white first screen, followed by cropped working camera and album fragments carrying `data-ui` as Visual design describes.

Islands in natural light
At the `full` preset the islands show a sun and sky following the world hour, soft shadows, water reflecting the sky and explorer, grass swaying and parting, fireflies at dusk, rain rings, and depth of field in photo mode.

Lens Up feels like a serious camera
Photo mode shows a stark framing guide whose corners turn red on a creature, equal-width readouts, depth of field following focus, moving shutter bars and a pinned `Scoring` thumbnail before the breakdown appears.

The dealt design on every working screen
The HUD, sheets, albums, boards, notice board, ranger queue and postcard form use Albert Sans on white with grey panels, near-square corners, equal-width figures, viewfinder empty states and solid black error bands, with red only on the shutter, focus lock and single action.

World and assets from the app's own code
Source shows three.js installed as a bundled dependency and every model, texture and sound generated by the app's code or shipped with a permitted licence and listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, with no remote asset reference.

Server-only scoring and environment credentials
Source shows score, frame acceptance for storage, weather and creature truth decided on the server with client-sent values ignored, and every service credential read from the environment and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build`, `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.
The application is written in TypeScript.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every shipped package and every bundled font, photograph or other asset not generated by the app, with its licence; "shipped packages" means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).
Shipped packages and bundled assets use only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, OFL or CC0 licences.
The only datastores are Postgres and MinIO, and the only mail path is Mailpit; no other database, queue or cache is added.
The page source references no remote script, font, image, model or sound.
No service worker, pointer lock, gamepad, WebXR or device sensor API appears in the source.
